source.transcribed: The vertex position and texture corner formulas come from data/shader/cube/quads13/cube-3rd.vsh and were rewritten in Java (ShapeDump.shaderPos); the game's own Java port of that shader, org.schema.game.client.view.Segment2ObjWriter.softwareShader, has the same arithmetic. Everything else is read from the game's classes at run time.

convention.coordinates: Unit cube, 0..1 on each axis = game block-local position + 0.5. x=1 is the +X face (Element.RIGHT), y=1 the +Y face (TOP), z=1 the +Z face (FRONT).
convention.winding: faces[].verts are ordered so that cross(v1-v0, v2-v0) points along `normal` (outward) in this right-handed x,y,z frame, i.e. counter-clockwise seen from outside. render[].verts keep the game's own emission order instead.
convention.side: faces[].side / sideId name the cube side the face lies in (Element constants); null for a diagonal face. `full` is true when the face is that entire unit square.
convention.sideCoverage: Per side id 0..5: 2 = the solid covers the whole square, 1 = part of it (a triangle), 0 = nothing.
convention.uv: render[].verts[].uv is the texture corner the game assigns: u = (ext >> 1) & 1, v = ext & 1, with texCoord = (tileColumn + u, tileRow + v) / 16. v grows in the same direction as the tile row index.
convention.orientationIndex: shapes[style].orientations is indexed by the block's stored 5 bit orientation value. The game looks an algorithm up with value % orientationModulus; values up to modulus-1 are listed.

blockBits.note: Current layout (segment version byte 3 and later, SegmentDataIntArray): the 5 orientation bits are used as they are; the active bit is not part of the orientation. Segment versions 0..2 used an older layout and are migrated on load (SegmentData3Byte.convertOrient: for corner, tetra, hepta and normal24 blocks new = (old4bits + (active ? 0 : 16)) % 24).

cube.textureSlots: ElementInformation.textureId[0..5] (the six ids in BlockConfig.xml, in order) are slots 0 FRONT, 1 BACK, 2 TOP, 3 BOTTOM, 4 RIGHT, 5 LEFT of the block itself. textureSlotByWorldSide[s] is the slot drawn on the face lying on world side s; worldSideBySlot[k] is the world side(s) slot k ends up on.

sixSided.orientationClamp: The mesher clamps the stored value to 0..5 for blocks with individualSides 6.

orientations.ownSideDirs: front (0,0,1) back (0,0,-1) top (0,1,0) bottom (0,-1,0) right-slot (-1,0,0) left-slot (1,0,0)
front (0,0,-1) back (0,0,1) top (0,1,0) bottom (0,-1,0) right-slot (1,0,0) left-slot (-1,0,0)
front (0,1,0) back (0,-1,0) top (-1,0,0) bottom (1,0,0) right-slot (0,0,1) left-slot (0,0,-1)
front (0,-1,0) back (0,1,0) top (1,0,0) bottom (-1,0,0) right-slot (0,0,-1) left-slot (0,0,1)
front (-1,0,0) back (1,0,0) top (0,1,0) bottom (0,-1,0) right-slot (0,0,1) left-slot (0,0,-1)
front (1,0,0) back (-1,0,0) top (0,1,0) bottom (0,-1,0) right-slot (0,0,-1) left-slot (0,0,1)

threeSided.orientationClamp: The mesher clamps the stored value to 0..5 for blocks with individualSides 3.

oneSided.note: individualSides 1: every face uses slot 0; the orientation only changes texture rotation (texOrder[style][orientation % 6]). The mesher does not clamp the value.

normal24.note: Style 6 (rails, rotators, display modules and similar). The mesher calls getOrientationCode24(side, orientation / 4), so the texture slots depend on the primary side only. orientationMatrix columns are right, up (= DIRECTIONS[primary]), forward (= DIRECTIONS[secondary]) as the game builds them; the Switched variant swaps LEFT and RIGHT first. lodBasis is the rotation the game applies to the block's LoD model (Oriencube.getBasicTransform); rows are listed, lodBasisUp/Forward are where the model's +Y and +Z axes end up.

texOrder.note: For plain cubes: texOrder[style][orientation % 6][side] lists, for the four vertices the mesher emits for that side, pos (unit cube) and uv (texture corner). NORMAL is used by default and always for three sided blocks (with orientation 0), ORIENT when the block has sideTexturesPointToOrientation, AREA4x4 for extended (4x4 tiled) textures.

slabs.note: Slab geometry as the mesher emits it for a cube style block: HalfBlockArray.getHalfBlockConfig moves vertices in quarter block steps. box is [minX,minY,minZ,maxX,maxY,maxZ] in unit cube coordinates.

handedness.note: Evidence about display handedness from the cube texture mapping, assuming texture tile row 0 is the top row of the atlas image (v grows downward in the image). If faces read normally in a right-handed view the game draws x,y,z right-handed, which puts +X on the viewer's left when looking along +Z (FRONT) with +Y up.

orientation0: FRONT: image right = (1,0,0), image up = (0,1,0) (reads normally in a right-handed view)
BACK: image right = (-1,0,0), image up = (0,1,0) (reads normally in a right-handed view)
TOP: image right = (-1,0,0), image up = (0,0,1) (reads normally in a right-handed view)

notes: Side ids: 0 FRONT +Z, 1 BACK -Z, 2 TOP +Y, 3 BOTTOM -Y, 4 RIGHT +X, 5 LEFT -X (Element.DIRECTIONSi). The mesher draws side 4 at +X.

LEFT and RIGHT are swapped in orientation semantics: for cube orientations, slabs and 24-orientation blocks the value named RIGHT (4) points to -X and LEFT (5) to +X (the game calls Element.switchLeftRight in these paths). FRONT, BACK, TOP, BOTTOM are as named. Wedge, corner, tetra and hepta geometry is given directly, so no swap has to be applied to it.

Lookup is algorithms[style-1][orientation % modulus] in physics and build code, but the mesher indexes algorithms[style-1][orientation] without the modulo, where index `modulus` is an icon placeholder. Write only values below the modulus.
Wedges repeat after 12 values, tetra and hepta after 8, sprites after 6; corners and normal24 use all 24. See checks.duplicateOrientations.
Sprites (style 3) are not solid: no hull, two crossed quads drawn from both sides; `render` lists the quads the mesher emits.
normal24 blocks (style 6) are full cubes for geometry; blocks with a LoD model (most rails) are drawn with that model rotated by lodBasis instead.

render[].emittedForSide is the cube side whose visibility triggers the quad; the slanted face of a wedge is emitted for its `angled` side. Entries with drawn=false are collapsed quads the game still sends to the GPU.

Only hepta blocks emit a seventh quad (emittedForSide 6, the diagonal face); the game sends it together with the side given in extraSideEmittedWith. Wedge, corner and tetra bend one of the six ordinary quads into the slanted face instead.

The mesher clamps the stored orientation to 0..5 for every block with individualSides 3 or 6 before it picks the shape algorithm, so the few non-cube blocks listed in styles[].blocksWithSeveralTextures can only be drawn in their first six orientations. Non-cube blocks with individualSides 1 use texture slot 0 on every face.
mirror.xy / xz / yz give the orientation value after mirroring across that plane (xy flips Z, xz flips Y, yz flips X), from BlockShapeAlgorithm.xyMappings etc.
Cargo space (id 689) reuses the orientation value as its slab height and block 689/688 have special default orientations; they are not covered here.

Hepta blocks cover three sides completely, but the game's getSidesToCheckForVis is empty for them, so the game never hides a neighbour's face behind a hepta. sideCoverage reports the geometry, not that choice.
Algorithm class names are not a reliable description (WedgeTopRight has its full wall on +X, WedgeBottomRight on -X); use faces and description.

Display handedness: tile rows in the block atlas count from the top of the image (checked by hand against t000.png: tile 20 is red, 22 yellow, 24 blue, matching the Standard Armor blocks), so v grows downward in the image and the `handedness` section applies: cube textures read unmirrored only if x,y,z are drawn as a right-handed frame.
Default orientation on placement (ElementInformation.getDefaultOrientation): 2 for sprites and three sided blocks, 14 for normal24, otherwise 0.
